title: Reduction of shock-wave data with mean-field potential approach
volume_normalization: dimensionless V/V0; no absolute V0 synthesized
model: generalized universal EOS with quartic exponent; do not treat it as ordinary two-coefficient Vinet
method: LAPW 0 K energy; MFP ion free energy plus electronic thermal free energy; calculated thermal volume increment subtracted at fixed pressure
exchange_correlation: GGA for Cu/Ta/Mo, LDA for Pt/Au (ref.15 footnote)
uncertainty: No coefficient covariance or fit intervals tabulated in Table II; model/data accuracy estimates in Sec.II.C are not pointwise standard deviations.
limitations: Shock melting and phase dependence neglected.
Authors explicitly distinguish this reduction from the theoretical curves of Moriarty and coworkers.
Original LAPW energy arrays, intermediate reduced samples, and Dewaele Vinet resampling/weights not recovered.
OCR_caution: Minus signs can be read as digit 2 in extracted text. All five coefficient rows and the Eq.8 powers were checked against rendered page 6618.
